# `$flow-work-daily $ARGUMENTS`

> **codex adapter — how the Claude Code primitives named below map here.**
> - `AskUserQuestion` → ask in plain text with numbered options and wait for the reply.
> - `Agent <role>` / `Agent general-purpose` / subagents → the subagent declared under `[agents.<name>]` in `~/.codex/config.toml`; the name comes from `agents.<role>` in `FLOW.md`, empty → do it in this context.
> - Parallel fan-out → several subagents in one response, capped at `agents.fanout_max` (empty → 4); `agents.fanout_tool` is Claude Code-only, ignore it.
> - `ScheduleWakeup` / `Monitor` / `/loop` → not available in-session: run one cycle, persist state in `monitor.md`, let the user schedule `codex exec "<command>"` with cron or Codex automations.
> - `TaskCreate` → a markdown checklist in the phase artifact.
> - `Skill commit-commands:commit-push-pr` → `git add` · `git commit` · `git push -u origin HEAD` · the `git.cli` CLI (`gh pr create` / `glab mr create`).
> - `/model <value>` → the `--model` flag at launch (or `/model` if your Codex version has it).
> - `knowledge.*` roles → whatever tools `FLOW.md` names there; an MCP tool keeps its name, its server is declared under `[mcp_servers.<name>]` in `config.toml` (see `config.snippet.toml`).
> - `$ARGUMENTS` → whatever the user typed after the skill name, empty if nothing — Codex substitutes nothing, so read it off their message.

Read `~/.claude/flow/CORE.codex.md` first (shared rules: `FLOW.md` step 0, autonomy, how a stop reads, the live panel, `00-summary.md`) — skip if you already read it in this session.

**Panel words are closed** — `mark`: `done` · `current` · `pending` · `wait` · `block` · `info`; `style`: `normal` · `dim` · `title` · `accent` · `ok` · `warn` · `error`. Anything else is dropped by the reader in silence: the panel still paints, and nobody is told.

External sources (tracker, forge, `knowledge`) are all **best-effort**: a CLI missing/unauthenticated, an MCP failing, or a call over ~3s → continue without that source and note it in a single line; **never block**.

Your **work assistant**: a Scrum-style daily standup — *"what was I working on?"*, *"what's left?"*, *"what should I pick up today?"* — from three sources: **local** work state, the **forge** (open MRs/PRs, reviews, CI), the **tracker** (assigned/re-prioritized tickets). The one overview of every open work; `$flow-work-resume` is the one-branch view. With forge and tracker both unavailable it is still the full local picture.

**Read-only.** Never touches `meta.json`, git, the forge, or the tracker; its only write is the "last seen" marker (§7). What it finds stale it reports and points at the command that writes.

## Modes

- **No `$ARGUMENTS`** → full daily briefing (§6).
- **`$ARGUMENTS` is a question** (e.g. `$flow-work-daily what's left on the payment work?`) → answer *that* from the same sources, without the full briefing. Do not move the marker (ad-hoc lookup, like `$flow-news vX.Y.Z`).

## 0. Who "you" are

Every *mine* below — your MRs/PRs, your threads, your tickets — is the **authenticated account** of each CLI, never a name. Two people can share a first name; a match on a display name hands one of them the other's work.

- **Forge**: `@me` in list filters. To compare authorship (§2 threads), resolve your login once — `gh api user --jq .login` · `glab api user` → `.username` — and compare it to each comment's author **username**, exactly. `git.assignee` overrides it only when set, and is an exact username too.
- **Tracker**: the tool's own self-reference — Jira `assignee = currentUser()` (JQL), `gh`/`glab` `--assignee @me`, Linear the viewer (`me`). `tracker.assignee` overrides it only when set, as an exact account id or email. Never build the filter from `git.assignee`: a forge username is not a tracker account.

## 1. Local layer (always — the base of the briefing)

- The work for this branch (flow-core §0) → the **active** work. From the main checkout on the base branch there is none — that is not "nothing in flight".
- Every work folder in both locations of flow-core §0, here and the main checkout (ignore `_archive`); read each `meta.json`. Name the worktree a work is checked out in (`git worktree list`) next to it, so the user knows where to `cd` (folders are `<TICKET>-<slug>`, `<slug>` for ticket-less works, or just `<TICKET>` for older ones — identify each by `meta.json.ticket`, not the folder name). Read `00-summary.md` per work when it exists and take the recap from it (`Next:` line, what is pending) instead of every artifact (flow-core §5); missing → the most recent artifact(s) (`NN-*.md`) and `meta.notes`, not re-derived from code.
- **"Last session" boundary**: the marker from §7 if present; otherwise the most recent commit date and the newest `updated_at` across works.
- Order works by `updated_at` (most recent first); the first is the *"what were we on?"* answer.
- Repo pulse: `git log --oneline --since="<last-session boundary>"` (fallback `-10`) and `git status --short` for uncommitted changes.
- Per work: `phase`, `phases_done`, MRs and their `status` (from `meta.json.mrs`), and what was **left pending**.
- **Cross-repo parts**: `meta.json.related_repos` entries not `done` → a *sibling repo* still needs work. Surface only what is recorded — never scan or open the other repo.
- **Roadmap** (flow-core §10): where the project stands, and which open work delivers which item. An unchecked item no open work links, ahead of the in-progress ones, is what to pick up next.
- **Open follow-ups**: `followups[]` entries not `declined`/`logged`/`done`, from the live works **and** from `_archive/*/meta.json` (flow-core §7). The archive is read for this and nothing else — a finished work is exactly when its deferred items stop being visible.
- **Measured cost**: `meta.json.cost[]` entries (flow-core §4) — sum the `usd` there, count the phases behind them, count apart the entries whose `source` is `not reported`. No entries → no figure at all: absence is not zero. The figures are the harness's client-side estimates, not a bill; `flow cost` prints them phase by phase.

### Current branch only (you can measure it)

When a work's `branch` is the current one. Base = `git.default_base` in FLOW.md; empty → auto-discover the repo's base branch.

- **Size vs estimate** of its `in_progress` MR/PR: `git diff --shortstat <base>..HEAD` and `git diff --name-only <base>..HEAD | wc -l` against `mrs[in_progress].lines_est` / `files_est`. Lines > `lines_est * 1.5` **or** files > `files_est + 2` → `⚠ exceeds estimate`, suggesting `$flow-feat-build` §2.3 (cut / continue / reopen). No `lines_est` → no line; never invent an estimate.
- **Log vs git**: files changed on the branch (`git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD`) against those listed in `05-implementation.md` (features) or `04-fix.md` (bugs). Changed but not logged, or logged with no change → `⚠ Divergence: <N> files not recorded in log (e.g. <path>, <path>)`.

### Orphans and residue

- Local branches matching `git.branch_pattern` (empty → `<prefix>XXXXX-*`) with no work folder claiming them via `meta.json.ticket`/`branch` → name them.
- Work folders whose branch no longer exists locally → candidates to archive (`$flow-work-clean`).
- **Residue** (one count, no per-entry detail): worktrees registered (`git worktree list`, minus the main checkout) whose work is `done` or that no work folder claims, work folders with `phase: done` still outside `_archive/`, and prunable registrations (`git worktree prune --dry-run`).

## 2. Forge layer (best-effort, via `git.cli`)

What the team is asking of you **right now**, and what already happened to the MRs/PRs your works recorded. Resolve the CLI from `git.cli` (or infer from `git.host`); "you" per §0.

- **Your open MRs/PRs**: `glab mr list --author=@me` / `gh pr list --author @me`.
- **Awaiting your review**: `glab mr list --reviewer=@me` / `gh pr list --search "review-requested:@me"`.
- **Recorded vs real state** — every `meta.json.mrs[]` entry with a number whose `status` is not `merged`/`closed`/`superseded`: one `glab mr view <n> --output json` / `gh pr view <n> --json state,mergedAt` each. The forge says merged or closed while the work still says otherwise → that work is **stale**: the merge happened outside flow, and the open-list above can no longer show it.
- **CI red** on your MRs/PRs → flag it (→ `$flow-work-green`).
- **Cannot merge** — the forge's verdict, distinct from the pipeline: conflicts, behind base, draft, approvals missing (`detailed_merge_status`/`has_conflicts` on GitLab · `mergeable`/`mergeStateStatus`/`reviewDecision` on GitHub). Flag separately, naming the reason. Conflicts / behind-base → `$flow-work-green`; draft and approvals are yours or the reviewers' to clear.
- **Threads that need *your* reply** — **latest comment not yours** (§0), fetched per open MR/PR (`glab api .../merge_requests/:iid/discussions` · `gh api` review threads). This — **not** the raw *unresolved* count — is the signal for `$flow-work-respond` (it **never resolves** threads, so an answered thread stays unresolved until the reviewer closes it).
- **Threads awaiting the reviewer** — unresolved, latest comment **is yours**: **informational only**, never an action for you.

Degrade: `git.cli` empty / not installed / unauthenticated / timeout → skip this layer and print one line, e.g. `(forge unavailable: gh not authenticated — MR/PR states are as last recorded)`. The term MR/PR follows `git.host` (`gitlab` → MR, otherwise PR).

## 3. Tracker layer (best-effort, via `tracker.tool`)

What you should **start or re-prioritize**. Resolve from `tracker.tool`; "you" per §0:

- **Assigned to you, not finished**:
  - Jira: `acli jira workitem search --jql "assignee = currentUser() AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY updated DESC" --json`
  - GitHub: `gh issue list --assignee @me` · GitLab: `glab issue list --assignee=@me`
  - Linear: its MCP when available, filtered by the viewer.
- Highlight: recently assigned, **priority changes**, and status changes that do not match your local work state.

Degrade like §2. `tracker.tool` `none`/empty → skip with one line (`(no tracker configured)`). Ticket format follows `tracker.prefix`.

## 4. Cross the three layers (the real value)

Turn the *joins* into concrete, **suggested** commands (never act):

- **A recorded MR/PR merged or closed on the forge** (§2) → the work's state is behind: `merged on the forge, work still says in progress`. Last MR/PR of the work → `$flow-work-clean` (it establishes the merged verdict and archives); more parts planned → `$flow-work-resume <TICKET>` picks up the next one.
- Ticket assigned to you with **no local work** → `$flow-feat-start <TICKET>` or `$flow-bug-start <TICKET>`.
- Local work `done`/`ship` but its ticket still open in the tracker → divergence to close out.
- Local work whose branch has an open MR/PR with **CI red or an unmergeable state** (conflicts, behind base) → `$flow-work-green`; with **threads awaiting your reply** (latest comment not yours) → `$flow-work-respond`.
- A ticket's **priority was raised** while you were on something else → call out the possible refocus.
- `related_repos` entries not `done` → the **other repo's part is still open**: surface it (`<repo>: <scope>`) and suggest `$flow-feat-start <TICKET>` in that repo. `contract_handoff` `pending` → add that the contract was never handed over; the fix is `$flow-feat-ship` §6.3 on this side first. flow only reminds; it never scans the sibling.
- **Follow-ups nobody has decided on** → one line at most, not a list: `<N> follow-ups awaiting a decision (oldest: <TICKET> F2 — <title>)`, and separately any `accepted` entry with no `work` started, suggesting `$flow-feat-start <ticket>`. A standup is where deferred work should resurface; it is not where it gets triaged — that is `ship`, once. Say nothing when there are none.
- Uncommitted local changes not reflected in any log/artifact → nudge toward the relevant phase.
- A `closed` MR/PR with no later decision recorded → the user decides: retry `$flow-feat-build` or `$flow-work-abandon`.
- `phase: abandoned` folder outside `_archive/` → it should have moved; `$flow-work-clean`.
- **Residue above a handful** → one line at the end: `Residue: <N> worktrees · <N> unarchived done · <N> prunable → $flow-work-clean --dry-run`. Housekeeping, never the headline; this command deletes nothing.
- **A mid-work knowledge save lives here.** `knowledge.read_staging` is set and returns entries for the current branch → offer, as one more next step, to consolidate them now (flow-core §0) instead of waiting for `ship` or `postmortem`. Only when there are entries, never as a question of its own: this is the last place a session about to end can bank what it learned.

Suggest only. The user decides.

## 5. In flight — one block per open work

The briefing's reference section: every open work, compact, most recently updated first.

```
<TICKET> — <title> [feat|bug] [XS|S|M|L]  ⏵ <phase>   [✓ current branch]
  MR/PRs:     2/4 merged · MR/PR #3 in_progress · MR/PR #4 pending
  Size:       180/120 lines (150%) · 7/6 files  ⚠ exceeds estimate     (current branch only)
  Cross-repo: <repo>: <scope> — contract not handed over                (only if any)
  Follow-ups: 2 awaiting a decision · 1 accepted, not started           (only if any)
  Cost:       $0.71 measured over 2 phases · 1 phase not reported       (only if any)
  Roadmap:    <phase › item it delivers>                                 (only if linked)
  Next:       <the concrete next command>
```

- `MR/PRs:` only with `meta.json.mrs` entries: `<merged>/<total> merged`, plus `closed`/`superseded` counts and the one `in_progress` by number; a closed or superseded one gets its reason (≤40 chars). A state corrected by the forge (§2) shows the **forge's** state, marked `(forge)`.
- `Follow-ups:` counts `proposed` as *awaiting a decision* and `accepted` without a `work` as *accepted, not started*; `in_progress` ones are their own work — never double-count.
- `Next:` from §4's joins first, else the work's own `Next:` from `00-summary.md`, else the phase after `phase`.

## 6. Output — the daily briefing (no `$ARGUMENTS`)

A short, narrative standup, then the reference block, then next steps:

```
☀ Daily — <repo> · since <last-session boundary>

Yesterday / last session
  <what you were on, what was left mid-way — 2-4 lines, most recent first>

Today
  <what to resume + what the forge/tracker asks of you, ordered by urgency>

Roadmap (only with one)
  <phase › milestone — done/total · in progress: item (work) · next: item>

Blockers / attention
  <CI red · reviews awaiting you (latest comment not yours) · stale works (merged on the forge) · divergences · raised priorities — or "none">

Awaiting others (optional)
  <threads you already answered, waiting on the reviewer — informational, not yours to act on>

In flight
  <§5, one block per open work>

Follow-ups awaiting a decision (optional)
  PROJ-123 F2  audit the other three callers of the same helper       (archived work)

Next: <2-4 concrete flow commands>
```

- Scannable prose, not a raw dump. Mark degraded sources inline so the user knows what was **not** checked (e.g. a trailing `(tracker unavailable)` line).
- **Blockers is only what *you* must act on.** Threads you already answered go in *Awaiting others*, never in Blockers — omit that block when empty.
- *Follow-ups awaiting a decision*: only when §4 found more than one; newest five and the total past about eight. Read-only — never triages, creates a ticket, or edits `followups[]`.
- No local works and no external items → say so plainly and suggest `$flow-feat-start` or `$flow-bug-start`.

## 7. "Last seen" marker (the only write)

Like `$flow-news`: a timestamp in `~/.claude/flow/daily-last-seen` (outside the repo) makes *"since last session"* precise.

- First run (no marker): derive the boundary from commits/`updated_at` (§1) and create the marker at the end.
- Update the marker **only** in the no-`$ARGUMENTS` briefing mode; untouched when answering an ad-hoc question.
- The documented exception to the read-only rule; everything else observes.
